subject: Background dots in the scatter plot matrix for hexagonal geom

messages.author: bd6e26d77fbee35a
messages.subject: Background dots in the scatter plot matrix for hexagonal geom
parts:
Hi,

The following codes generate a scatter plot matrix with hexagonal
geom. It also plots the black dots in the background. Since I have
several million records, I really don't want those dots to be printed.

library(ggplot2)
n <- 1000
x <- rnorm(n)
y <- 3+2*x+rnorm(n)
z <- 2 + x*y
plotmatrix(data.frame(x,y,z))+stat_binhex(bins=25)

Now I have two questions.
1. Is there any way to get rid of those background dots?
2. Can't I do it using my favorite ggplot() function using some
geom_layout="matrix_plot"? At least my mind is set to the grammar used
by ggplot2 and I am having a hard time using plotmatrix() function.

Any help will be highly appreciated. I am using Linux (R-2.11.1).

Thanks.

--
Mahbub Majumder
Graduate Student
Dept. of Statistics
Iowa State University

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: Background dots in the scatter plot matrix for hexagonal geom
parts: > 1. Is there any way to get rid of those background dots?

you can do it by modifying plotmatrix function itself. please find the
code below.

> 2. Can't I do it using my favorite ggplot() function using some
> geom_layout="matrix_plot"? At least my mind is set to the grammar used
> by ggplot2 and I am having a hard time using plotmatrix() function.

maybe a good idea, but acutally plotmatrix do more than arranging the layout.


here is an example:

n <- 5

d1 <- data.frame(x, y, z)

idx <- subset(expand.grid(names(d1), names(d1)), Var1!=Var2)
dh <- do.call("rbind", apply(idx, 1, function(i)data.frame(v1=i[1],
v2=i[2], x1=c(d1[[i[1]]]), x2=c(d1[[i[2]]]))))
dd <- with(melt(d1), data.frame(v1=variable, v2=variable, x=value))

ggplot() +
stat_density(aes(x, y = ..scaled.. * diff(range(x)) + min(x)), dd,
geom="line") +
stat_binhex(aes(x1, x2), dh, bind=25) +
facet_grid(v1~v2, scales = "free")


--

messages.subject: Re: Background dots in the scatter plot matrix for hexagonal geom
parts:
Thanks for your reply. Your codes gave some warning like 'ymax not
defined' with my real data. But inspired by your solution I just
modified (replaced geom_point by stat_binhex) the plotmatrix function
as below which works fine with my data.

modified_plotmatrix <- function (data, mapping = aes(), colour = "black")
{
grid <- expand.grid(x = 1:ncol(data), y = 1:ncol(data))
grid <- subset(grid, x != y)
all <- do.call("rbind", lapply(1:nrow(grid), function(i) {
xcol <- grid[i, "x"]
ycol <- grid[i, "y"]
data.frame(xvar = names(data)[ycol], yvar = names(data)[xcol],
x = data[, xcol], y = data[, ycol], data)
}))
all$xvar <- factor(all$xvar, levels = names(data))
all$yvar <- factor(all$yvar, levels = names(data))
densities <- do.call("rbind", lapply(1:ncol(data), function(i) {
data.frame(xvar = names(data)[i], yvar = names(data)[i],
x = data[, i])
}))
mapping <- plyr::defaults(mapping, aes_string(x = "x", y = "y"))
class(mapping) <- "uneval"
ggplot(all,mapping) +
stat_binhex(bins=20,na.rm = TRUE) +
stat_density(aes(x = x,y = ..scaled.. * diff(range(x)) +
min(x)), data = densities,
position = "identity", colour = "grey20", geom = "line") +
facet_grid(xvar ~ yvar, scales = "free")
}

modified_plotmatrix(d1)

Again, many thanks for your time on this.
